"""Focused graph-depth contract; prepared before the iterative implementation."""
import hashlib
import json
import sys
import unittest

from fanout_engine.plan import Part, Plan, PlanError


CHAIN_PARTS = 1536


def encoded_document(document):
    """Independent public identity formula, not the product serializer."""
    return json.dumps(
        document, sort_keys=True, separators=(",", ":"),
        ensure_ascii=False, allow_nan=False,
    ).encode("utf-8")


def chain_document(*, reverse=False, cycle=False):
    """Fixed finite input: increasing-index edges, optionally one back edge."""
    rows = []
    for index in range(CHAIN_PARTS):
        dependencies = [f"n{index + 1:04d}"] if index + 1 < CHAIN_PARTS else []
        if cycle and index + 1 == CHAIN_PARTS:
            dependencies = ["n0768"]
        rows.append({
            "id": f"n{index:04d}",
            "instruction": f"Step {index}.",
            "depends_on": dependencies,
            "tags": [],
        })
    if reverse:
        rows.reverse()
    return {"project": "depth-chain", "parts": rows}


class PlanAcyclicDepthTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        self.recursion_limit_before = sys.getrecursionlimit()

    def tearDown(self):
        self.assertEqual(sys.getrecursionlimit(), self.recursion_limit_before)

    def assert_plan_identity(self, plan, expected):
        self.assertEqual(plan.to_dict(), expected)
        digest = hashlib.sha256(encoded_document(expected)).hexdigest()
        self.assertEqual(plan.digest, digest)
        ids = [expected["parts"][0]["id"], expected["parts"][-1]["id"]]
        for part_id in dict.fromkeys(ids):
            material = (
                expected["project"] + "\0" + digest + "\0" + part_id
            ).encode("utf-8")
            self.assertEqual(
                plan.idempotency_key(part_id),
                "fanout-" + hashlib.sha256(material).hexdigest(),
            )

    def construct(self, document, expected=None):
        before = encoded_document(document)
        if expected is None:
            expected = json.loads(before)
        plan = Plan.from_dict(document)
        self.assertEqual(encoded_document(document), before)
        self.assert_plan_identity(plan, expected)
        return plan

    def refuse(self, document, message):
        before = encoded_document(document)
        with self.assertRaises(PlanError) as caught:
            Plan.from_dict(document)
        self.assertIs(type(caught.exception), PlanError)
        self.assertEqual(str(caught.exception), message)
        self.assertEqual(encoded_document(document), before)

    def test_dependent_first_long_chain(self):
        plan = self.construct(chain_document())
        self.assertEqual(tuple(p.id for p in plan.ready_parts()), ("n1535",))
        self.assertEqual(
            tuple(p.id for p in plan.ready_parts({"n1535"})),
            ("n1534", "n1535"),
        )

    def test_prerequisite_first_long_chain(self):
        plan = self.construct(chain_document(reverse=True))
        self.assertEqual(tuple(p.id for p in plan.ready_parts()), ("n1535",))
        self.assertEqual(
            tuple(p.id for p in plan.ready_parts({"n1535"})),
            ("n1535", "n1534"),
        )

    def test_declaration_order_keeps_distinct_representation_and_identity(self):
        rows = [
            {"id": "tip", "instruction": "Tip.", "depends_on": ["right", "left"], "tags": []},
            {"id": "left", "instruction": "Left.", "depends_on": ["base"], "tags": []},
            {"id": "right", "instruction": "Right.", "depends_on": ["base"], "tags": []},
            {"id": "base", "instruction": "Base.", "depends_on": [], "tags": []},
        ]
        first = self.construct({"project": "order", "parts": rows})
        second = self.construct({"project": "order", "parts": list(reversed(rows))})
        self.assertNotEqual(first.digest, second.digest)
        self.assertNotEqual(first.idempotency_key("tip"), second.idempotency_key("tip"))
        self.assertEqual(first.parts[0].depends_on, ("right", "left"))
        self.assertEqual(second.parts[-1].depends_on, ("right", "left"))
        self.assertEqual(tuple(p.id for p in first.ready_parts()), ("base",))
        self.assertEqual(tuple(p.id for p in second.ready_parts()), ("base",))

    def test_completed_shared_dependency_is_not_an_active_ancestor(self):
        document = {"project": "shared", "parts": [
            {"id": "tip", "instruction": "Tip.", "depends_on": ["right", "left"], "tags": []},
            {"id": "left", "instruction": "Left.", "depends_on": ["base"], "tags": []},
            {"id": "orphan", "instruction": "Orphan.", "depends_on": [], "tags": []},
            {"id": "right", "instruction": "Right.", "depends_on": ["base"], "tags": []},
            {"id": "base", "instruction": "Base.", "depends_on": [], "tags": []},
        ]}
        plan = self.construct(document)
        self.assertEqual(tuple(p.id for p in plan.ready_parts()), ("orphan", "base"))
        self.assertEqual(
            tuple(p.id for p in plan.ready_parts({"base"})),
            ("left", "orphan", "right", "base"),
        )

    def test_long_path_into_cycle_raises_native_plan_error(self):
        self.refuse(chain_document(cycle=True), "dependency graph contains a cycle")

    def test_later_disconnected_cycle_is_still_visited(self):
        document = chain_document(reverse=True)
        document["project"] = "later-cycle"
        document["parts"].extend([
            {"id": "loop_a", "instruction": "A.", "depends_on": ["loop_b"], "tags": []},
            {"id": "loop_b", "instruction": "B.", "depends_on": ["loop_a"], "tags": []},
        ])
        self.refuse(document, "dependency graph contains a cycle")

    def test_cycle_in_nonfirst_dependency_is_still_visited(self):
        document = {"project": "later-edge", "parts": [
            {"id": "tip", "instruction": "Tip.", "depends_on": ["base", "loop_a"], "tags": []},
            {"id": "base", "instruction": "Base.", "depends_on": [], "tags": []},
            {"id": "loop_a", "instruction": "A.", "depends_on": ["loop_b"], "tags": []},
            {"id": "loop_b", "instruction": "B.", "depends_on": ["loop_a"], "tags": []},
        ]}
        self.refuse(document, "dependency graph contains a cycle")

    def test_existing_validation_precedes_cycle_walk(self):
        cycle = [
            {"id": "a", "instruction": "A.", "depends_on": ["b"], "tags": []},
            {"id": "b", "instruction": "B.", "depends_on": ["a"], "tags": []},
        ]
        cases = [
            ("project", "not a project", [], "invalid project identifier"),
            ("duplicate_id", "precedence", [
                {"id": "a", "instruction": "Again.", "depends_on": [], "tags": []},
            ], "part identifiers must be unique"),
            ("instruction", "precedence", [
                {"id": "late", "instruction": " ", "depends_on": [], "tags": []},
            ], "each part needs a non-empty instruction"),
            ("duplicate_dependency", "precedence", [
                {"id": "late", "instruction": "Late.", "depends_on": ["a", "a"], "tags": []},
            ], "dependencies must be unique"),
            ("self_dependency", "precedence", [
                {"id": "late", "instruction": "Late.", "depends_on": ["late"], "tags": []},
            ], "a part cannot depend on itself"),
            ("unknown_dependency", "precedence", [
                {"id": "late", "instruction": "Late.", "depends_on": ["missing"], "tags": []},
            ], "a dependency references an unknown part"),
            ("tag", "precedence", [
                {"id": "late", "instruction": "Late.", "depends_on": [], "tags": ["bad tag"]},
            ], "invalid tag"),
        ]
        for label, project, extra, message in cases:
            with self.subTest(label=label):
                self.refuse({"project": project, "parts": cycle + extra}, message)

    def test_direct_lists_stay_detached_without_reordering_or_copying_parts(self):
        dependencies = ["right", "left"]
        tags = ["zeta", "alpha", "zeta"]
        tip = Part("tip", "Tip.", dependencies, tags)
        left = Part("left", "Left.")
        right = Part("right", "Right.")
        parts = [tip, left, right]
        plan = Plan("direct", parts)
        expected = {"project": "direct", "parts": [
            {"id": "tip", "instruction": "Tip.", "depends_on": ["right", "left"],
             "tags": ["zeta", "alpha", "zeta"]},
            {"id": "left", "instruction": "Left.", "depends_on": [], "tags": []},
            {"id": "right", "instruction": "Right.", "depends_on": [], "tags": []},
        ]}
        dependencies.clear()
        tags[:] = ["changed"]
        parts.clear()
        self.assertIsInstance(plan.parts, tuple)
        self.assertIs(plan.parts[0], tip)
        self.assertIs(plan.parts[1], left)
        self.assertIs(plan.parts[2], right)
        self.assertEqual(tip.depends_on, ("right", "left"))
        self.assertEqual(tip.tags, ("zeta", "alpha", "zeta"))
        self.assert_plan_identity(plan, expected)
        self.assertEqual(tuple(p.id for p in plan.ready_parts()), ("left", "right"))

    def test_from_dict_keeps_its_existing_tag_normalization(self):
        document = {"project": "normalized", "parts": [
            {"id": "tip", "instruction": "Tip.", "depends_on": ["right", "left"],
             "tags": ["zeta", "alpha", "zeta"]},
            {"id": "left", "instruction": "Left."},
            {"id": "right", "instruction": "Right."},
        ]}
        expected = {"project": "normalized", "parts": [
            {"id": "tip", "instruction": "Tip.", "depends_on": ["right", "left"],
             "tags": ["alpha", "zeta"]},
            {"id": "left", "instruction": "Left.", "depends_on": [], "tags": []},
            {"id": "right", "instruction": "Right.", "depends_on": [], "tags": []},
        ]}
        plan = self.construct(document, expected)
        document["parts"][0]["depends_on"].clear()
        document["parts"][0]["tags"].clear()
        document["parts"].clear()
        self.assert_plan_identity(plan, expected)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()

"""Plan validation and deterministic identity helpers."""
from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass, field
import hashlib
import json
import re
from typing import Any, Iterable

_IDENTIFIER = re.compile(r"[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9._-]{0,63}\Z")


class PlanError(ValueError):
    """Raised when a plan is malformed or internally inconsistent."""


def canonical_json(value: Any) -> str:
    """Serialize JSON deterministically and reject non-JSON numeric values."""
    try:
        return json.dumps(
            value, sort_keys=True, separators=(",", ":"),
            ensure_ascii=False, allow_nan=False,
        )
    except (TypeError, ValueError) as exc:
        raise PlanError("value is not canonical JSON") from exc


def strict_json_loads(text: str) -> Any:
    """Parse JSON while rejecting duplicate object keys and non-finite numbers."""
    def object_pairs(pairs: list[tuple[str, Any]]) -> dict[str, Any]:
        result: dict[str, Any] = {}
        for key, value in pairs:
            if key in result:
                raise PlanError("duplicate JSON object key")
            result[key] = value
        return result

    def invalid_constant(_: str) -> Any:
        raise PlanError("non-finite JSON number")

    try:
        return json.loads(text, object_pairs_hook=object_pairs, parse_constant=invalid_constant)
    except PlanError:
        raise
    except (TypeError, json.JSONDecodeError) as exc:
        raise PlanError("invalid JSON document") from exc


def _identifier(value: Any, label: str) -> str:
    if not isinstance(value, str) or not _IDENTIFIER.fullmatch(value):
        raise PlanError(f"invalid {label}")
    return value


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Part:
    id: str
    instruction: str
    depends_on: tuple[str, ...] = ()
    tags: tuple[str, ...] = ()

    def __post_init__(self) -> None:
        object.__setattr__(self, "depends_on", tuple(self.depends_on))
        object.__setattr__(self, "tags", tuple(self.tags))

    def to_dict(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
        return {
            "id": self.id,
            "instruction": self.instruction,
            "depends_on": list(self.depends_on),
            "tags": list(self.tags),
        }


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Plan:
    project_id: str
    parts: tuple[Part, ...]
    digest: str = field(init=False)

    def __post_init__(self) -> None:
        object.__setattr__(self, "parts", tuple(self.parts))
        _identifier(self.project_id, "project identifier")
        if not self.parts:
            raise PlanError("a plan must contain at least one part")
        ids = [part.id for part in self.parts]
        if len(ids) != len(set(ids)):
            raise PlanError("part identifiers must be unique")
        known = set(ids)
        for part in self.parts:
            _identifier(part.id, "part identifier")
            if not isinstance(part.instruction, str) or not part.instruction.strip():
                raise PlanError("each part needs a non-empty instruction")
            if len(part.depends_on) != len(set(part.depends_on)):
                raise PlanError("dependencies must be unique")
            if part.id in part.depends_on:
                raise PlanError("a part cannot depend on itself")
            if not set(part.depends_on) <= known:
                raise PlanError("a dependency references an unknown part")
            for tag in part.tags:
                _identifier(tag, "tag")
        self._check_acyclic()
        encoded = canonical_json(self.to_dict()).encode("utf-8")
        object.__setattr__(self, "digest", hashlib.sha256(encoded).hexdigest())

    @classmethod
    def from_dict(cls, value: Any) -> "Plan":
        if not isinstance(value, dict) or set(value) != {"project", "parts"}:
            raise PlanError("plan must contain exactly project and parts")
        project = _identifier(value["project"], "project identifier")
        raw_parts = value["parts"]
        if not isinstance(raw_parts, list):
            raise PlanError("parts must be a list")
        parts: list[Part] = []
        for item in raw_parts:
            if not isinstance(item, dict):
                raise PlanError("each part must be an object")
            allowed = {"id", "instruction", "depends_on", "tags"}
            if set(item) - allowed or not {"id", "instruction"} <= set(item):
                raise PlanError("part has missing or unexpected fields")
            part_id = _identifier(item["id"], "part identifier")
            deps = item.get("depends_on", [])
            tags = item.get("tags", [])
            if not isinstance(deps, list) or not all(isinstance(x, str) for x in deps):
                raise PlanError("depends_on must be a list of identifiers")
            if not isinstance(tags, list) or not all(isinstance(x, str) for x in tags):
                raise PlanError("tags must be a list of identifiers")
            parts.append(Part(part_id, item["instruction"], tuple(deps), tuple(sorted(set(tags)))))
        return cls(project, tuple(parts))

    def to_dict(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
        return {"project": self.project_id, "parts": [part.to_dict() for part in self.parts]}

    def _check_acyclic(self) -> None:
        graph = {part.id: part.depends_on for part in self.parts}
        visiting: set[str] = set()
        visited: set[str] = set()

        for node in graph:
            if node in visited:
                continue
            visiting.add(node)
            stack = [(node, iter(graph[node]))]
            while stack:
                current, parents = stack[-1]
                parent = next(parents, None)
                if parent is None:
                    stack.pop()
                    visiting.remove(current)
                    visited.add(current)
                elif parent in visiting:
                    raise PlanError("dependency graph contains a cycle")
                elif parent not in visited:
                    visiting.add(parent)
                    stack.append((parent, iter(graph[parent])))

    def ready_parts(self, completed: Iterable[str] = ()) -> tuple[Part, ...]:
        done = set(completed)
        return tuple(part for part in self.parts if set(part.depends_on) <= done)

    def idempotency_key(self, part_id: str) -> str:
        _identifier(part_id, "part identifier")
        if part_id not in {part.id for part in self.parts}:
            raise PlanError("unknown part identifier")
        material = f"{self.project_id}\0{self.digest}\0{part_id}".encode("utf-8")
        return "fanout-" + hashlib.sha256(material).hexdigest()
